study.question: Does jointly narrowing historical action and item representations recover the unusually poor native item8/action16 result while reducing parameters and measured inference cost relative to the source, with supplied context held at16?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g1-r0013-id8_attr8 (all six item fields8, action/context16) scored click AUC0.651350616 versus0.660646940 for g1-r0013-id16_attr16. Individual ID/attribute reductions scored0.658232857/0.659659304. This nonlinear joint loss is unresolved. Earlier uniform-width8 and copy-expanded8 trials scored0.657781850 and0.659116842, but also changed context and/or layout, so they cannot identify an action effect. Provisional mechanism: the relative action/item capacity presented to the shared activation and readouts can interact with compact item representations; jointly narrowing action may improve quality beyond an additive action effect while retaining compact item storage. This is a test of a width interaction, not proof of semantic action dominance or a new architecture. Initializations, optimizer trajectories, Dice state and dense fan-in are live alternatives. AUC retention and actual cost improvement are separate requirements.

study.proposed_difference: A complete 2x2 factorial over uniform item width{8,16} and historical action width{8,16}, with context16 in every cell. Narrow action in lookup, scorer input and pooled readout together. No projections, duplicated coordinates, new loss, new labels or new input information. The item8/action16 and full16 cells are exact-width construction controls for prior committed endpoints. This is an empirical capacity-allocation follow-up, with architectural novelty unverified and not claimed.
predictions: Let A(i,a) denote full-population click AUC for item width i/action width a. The predeclared interaction is D=[A(8,8)-A(8,16)]-[A(16,8)-A(16,16)]. D>0 and A(8,8)>A(8,16) would be preliminary directional evidence that action narrowing is more helpful with compact items; one seed is insufficient mechanism confirmation.

The two action16 controls should reproduce prior point metrics: A(8,16)=0.651350616000785 and A(16,16)=0.660646940486458. Same-seed replay validates construction, not independent replication. Investigate a discrepancy before interpreting the factorial.

Predeclared practical efficiency screen: compact AUC>=contemporaneous full16 AUC-0.0005; >=25% fewer total parameters; and >=5% lower model-only median batch latency, with p95 and end-to-end inference seconds also reported. These margins are operational screens, not significance/equivalence tests. Retention without uncertainty remains provisional.

Native item8 cells should have about19.86M parameters versus32.06M full16, conditional on released alias/vocabulary layout. Action-only narrowing has very small sparse savings and is an attribution control rather than a useful storage intervention.

Report all four task AUC/logloss, auxiliary mean separately, train/allocation/wall cost, peak memory, throughput and latency; compare inherited baseline and unchanged source. Use existing history bins and counts/positive/negative counts, emphasizing whether the long-history loss of the narrow-item control recovers. Slice analysis is exploratory.
falsifiers: D<=0 or A(8,8)<=A(8,16) fails the predicted direction for this implementation; it does not establish universal absence of action/item interaction.
If the compact cell fails the AUC retention margin or the parameter/latency screens, this round does not demonstrate the proposed practical efficiency benefit even if D>0.
If action narrowing helps both item widths equally, only an action main effect is supported; if repeats reverse D, the interaction remains unsupported.
Endpoint reconstruction, alias, masking, causality, finite probability/loss or gradient gates failing blocks scientific interpretation; retain and charge failed attempts.
alternative_explanations: Width changes consume a different RNG stream and alter dense fan-in; deterministic replay is not a second seed and cannot distinguish rank/capacity from initialization.
Dice/BatchNorm state and unnormalized pooled magnitude, optimizer conditioning and one-pass convergence could explain width interactions rather than relative semantic action information.
The old compact versus new native comparison changes context and representation layout, and is motivation only; no cross-trajectory causal estimate is taken from it.
ID/attribute width findings were not parameter matched. This factorial also changes sparse rank and dense input size together. Positive D does not identify which internal path mediates it.
GPU alignment, loading variance and clock noise can make fewer parameters fail to reduce measured inference cost. End-to-end and model-only timings must remain distinct.

Latest knowledge-usage declares Zenith-inspired ID/attribute separation but that prior executed factorial did not establish robust retention; EST was only considered. Neither supplies local action-width evidence or mandates this experiment.

The inherited source improves click over baseline-din (0.660646940 versus0.655544082) while auxiliary AUCs are substantially lower (source cart/fav/buy0.664153/0.709596/0.668801 versus baseline0.849070/0.864897/0.870182). Click selection must not be reported as overall four-task superiority; publish every task and preserve this tradeoff.
